criteria.criterion: Event level: mean net abnormal 15d return
criteria.threshold: mean > 0 and 95% CI lower bound > 0 (n >= 30 and >= 30 effective month clusters)

criteria.criterion: Excess over placebo (events minus placebo, month clusters resampled jointly)
criteria.threshold: difference > 0 and 95% CI lower bound > 0 (n >= 30 and >= 30 effective month clusters)

criteria.criterion: Walk-forward OUT-OF-SAMPLE mean net abnormal 15d return
criteria.threshold: mean > 0 and 95% CI lower bound > 0 (n >= 30 and >= 30 effective month clusters)

criteria.criterion: Placebo: mean abnormal 15d return on random non-event member days (before the fixed round-trip cost)
Stability: sub-periods with a positive mean

readings: Criterion 3 is judged on the placebo's abnormal 15d return BEFORE the fixed 10 bp round-trip cost (a constant cost would push any clean placebo below zero).
'Date-clustered' CIs resample calendar-month clusters (M), 2000 percentile-bootstrap replications.

Walk-forward: on each fit window the threshold with the highest i.i.d. t-score among those with >= 30 purged fit events is chosen; a window where none qualifies adds no test events. Purged = the fit event's 15d exit date falls before the test window opens.
Same-ticker events within 15 trading days of the last kept event are suppressed.
Criterion 4: at least 2 of the 3 sub-periods have a positive mean; a sub-period with no events counts as not positive.
Criteria 1, 1b and 2 also require n >= 30 and >= 30 effective month clusters: a low-confidence estimate never passes.

Placebo: the same tickers, one draw per event, from member days with finite model inputs and as-traded price >= $5, inside the events' date span, excluding each real event day and the 15 days after it. Days BEFORE an event are not excluded: that would keep only placebo windows with no future drop in them (lookahead).

Entries that are not real t+1 opens are missing data (volume[t+1] == 0 or as-traded open[t+1] == close[t]), for events and placebo alike; they are counted by year and the unfiltered mean is reported as a sensitivity row.
Events or placebo days whose stock or ETF price is missing at entry or exit are excluded from every mean and counted; they are never booked as losses or gains.

Placebo drift diagnostic (placebo abnormal return minus 15 x the ticker's mean daily abnormal return over the development window) is reported only. It does not change criterion 3 or the run's validity.

BETA_MIN_OBS.rationale: Minimum valid days inside the beta window before a fit is trusted.

BETA_WINDOW.rationale: Thesis: rolling 60-90d betas; upper end for estimate stability.

CLUSTER_FREQ.rationale: Calendar-month date clusters: wider than the 15d primary horizon, so overlapping forward windows and crash-clustered events mostly share a cluster.

COST_BPS_PER_SIDE.rationale: Conservative half-spread + slippage for S&P 500 names, per side.

ENTRY.rationale: Signal is known at close t; first tradable price is the t+1 open.

EVENT_COOLDOWN.rationale: Suppress same-ticker events inside the primary horizon to avoid double counting.

EVENT_Z_GRID.rationale: Only thresholds the walk-forward selector may choose between.

EXPANDING_MIN_OBS.rationale: Minimum history before an expanding-window quantile is defined.

FACTOR_N_BUCKETS.rationale: Terciles for one-factor-at-a-time tests: two cut points, the fewest that still separate high from low.

FDR_Q.rationale: Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery rate across one-factor-at-a-time tests.

HORIZONS.rationale: Thesis: forward returns at 1, 5, 15, 30 trading days.

MACRO_FFILL_LIMIT.rationale: Bridge holiday-calendar mismatches between sources only; longer gaps stay NaN so stale macro is never used.

MACRO_START_YEAR.rationale: Two years of warm-up before dev_start (2000) so trailing macro features are defined from day one.

MIN_EFFECTIVE_CLUSTERS.rationale: Kish effective number of date clusters, (sum c_g)^2 / sum c_g^2, below which cluster-robust CIs and p-values are anti-conservative (few-cluster guidance of ~20-50, Cameron & Miller 2015); such results are flagged low-confidence, matching the 30-instance rule.

MIN_PRICE.rationale: Exclude sub-$5 prints where spreads and tick size dominate returns.

MIN_SAMPLE_FINDING.rationale: Thesis: under ~30 instances is low-confidence, not a finding.

PANEL_WARMUP_DAYS.rationale: Calendar days loaded before dev_start: SECTOR_WINDOW + BETA_WINDOW = 342 trading days (~495 calendar days) of warm-up plus a holiday buffer.

PRIMARY_HORIZON.rationale: Pre-registered primary horizon (thesis worked example uses 15d).

REUSE_TOLERANCE_DAYS.rationale: A member cannot predate its first trade: a price history starting more than ~5 trading days after a membership spell begins marks the symbol as reused by another company, and that spell's prices are dropped.

SECTOR_REASSIGN_FREQ.rationale: Sector assignment refreshed month-end using only prior data.

SECTOR_WINDOW.rationale: One trading year of history to pick each stock's sector ETF.

SEC_NEWS_WINDOW.rationale: News effective the prior session can still drive day-t moves, so day t is flagged for effective dates t and t-1.

STABILITY_MIN_SUBPERIODS.rationale: Pre-registered: the mean must have H1's (positive) sign in at least 2 of the 3 sub-periods.

STALE_OPEN_RULE.rationale: An entry print that is not a real t+1 opening trade (no volume, or a free-data open copied from the prior close, ~10-15% of post-drop S&P bars before 2008 vs ~1-2% after) is missing data, not a fill; using it would silently turn the pre-registered next-open entry into a close entry, which favours H1.

STALE_WINDOW_SHARES.rationale: Shares of exactly-zero returns in a fit window above which the window is mostly stale prices (halt, illiquidity) and the rolling sigma is deflated, so z = resid/sigma can spike and manufacture fake events.

SUBPERIODS.rationale: Pre-registered stability split (criterion 4): three ~8-year calendar blocks fixed before any result.

SUSPICIOUS_SHARPE.rationale: Thesis: Sharpe above ~2-3 is treated as a probable bug until proven otherwise.

drift_adjusted.label: placebo abn_15 minus 15 x ticker mean daily abnormal return
